steps.body: Sticks build shapes the honest way: each stick one side, each meeting one corner. A triangle takes three sticks, a square four equal ones.
steps.narration: Sticks build shapes the honest way: each stick one side, each meeting one corner. A triangle takes three sticks, a square four equal ones.

widget.prompt: Check a second stick for the square. Start at zero and cover it with 4 equal unit blocks.
widget.successFeedback: 4 equal blocks cover the stick exactly — a side is a length, and the block count names it.
widget.alignFeedback: Line up zero with the object's starting end before measuring.
widget.gapOverlapFeedback: The blocks must touch end to end — no spaces and no covering the same part twice.
widget.unitFeedback: Every block must be the same size, or the count means nothing.

predict.prompt: Two sticks only — can they close into a shape?
predict.reveal: Two straight sticks can meet at most at their ends and leave the rest open; closing needs a third.

cml.actionGoal: Name shapes by sides and corners, place them with position words, and compose them edge to edge for kgb build shape.
invariants: A shape's name lives in its sides and corners — not its size, pose, or color; position words compare a thing to a landmark; and shapes joined edge to edge compose a larger whole — the anchors for kgb build shape.
misconceptions: Renaming a turned or resized shape, using position words without a landmark, or treating shapes as unjoinable.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If the shape were turned upside down, which of its sides or corners would disappear?

widget.prompt: Building a square from sticks — what must the sticks be?

options.label: Four sticks, all the same length
options.feedback: Correct — the square's four equal sides demand four equal sticks, corner to corner.

options.label: Any four sticks
options.feedback: Unequal sticks build a lopsided quadrilateral; EQUAL is part of square.

options.label: Three long sticks
options.feedback: Three sides close into a triangle; the square needs a fourth.

options.label: As many as possible
options.feedback: Extra sticks make extra sides — a pentagon, a hexagon, not a square.

widget.prompt: Count the sticks: start at 3 and count on 1. Tap where you land.

commonLandings.feedback: That stops one complete hop too soon. Continue the final 1-unit hop to reach 4.
That goes one complete hop too far. Count exactly 1 hops from 3.

widget.missFeedback: Count 1 on from 3: you land on 4.
widget.successFeedback: 4 — each stick takes one hop, and the landing is the count.
widget.lowFeedback: Short of the landing — all 1 counts are needed to reach 4.
widget.highFeedback: Past the landing — the count stops after 1 hops, on 4.

widget.prompt: Four equal sticks make a square. Slide the whole shape to a new spot. What is it now?

options.label: Still a square
options.feedback: Yes. Sliding changes the place, but the 4 equal sides still make a square.

options.label: A rectangle with unequal sides
options.feedback: No stick changed length, so all 4 sides are still equal.

options.label: A triangle
options.feedback: The 4 sticks stayed joined. A triangle would have only 3 sides.

options.label: No shape at all
options.feedback: The sticks stayed joined in a closed outline, so the square is still there.

widget.prompt: Which set of sticks can close to make a triangle?

options.label: 3 sticks joined end to end
options.feedback: Yes. Three sticks can meet end to end and close with 3 corners.

options.label: 2 sticks joined at one end
options.feedback: Two sticks leave an open angle. One more stick is needed to close it.

options.label: 4 sticks joined in a row
options.feedback: A row stays open, and 4 sides would make a different closed shape.

options.label: 1 stick by itself
options.feedback: One stick is only one side. A triangle needs 3 joined sides.
